body.statement: There exists a single finite \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{SI}}\subset\Lambda_{\mathrm{SI}}\), with rule schemata independent of \(D\) and \(K\), such that for every \(\eta\in\mathfrak M_{D,K}^{\mathrm{Dai}}\), \(\operatorname{Cl}_{\mathcal R}(\mathcal O(\eta))=\mathcal P_{\mathrm{SI}}(\mathcal O(\eta))\) on \(\mathcal E(\mathcal O(\eta))\). The input \(\mathcal O(\eta)\) is the full collection of regime-MAG adjacencies and unshielded colliders on \(U_k\): the observational component on \(U_0=V\) is associated with \(P_{\eta}^{(0)}=\mathcal L_{\eta}(X\mid S^*=\mathbf 1)\), and every \(k\in[K]\) regime MAG is the faithful graphical law of \(P_{\eta,k}^{\mathrm{pool}}\) on \(X\cup\{\zeta_k\}\), including all \(\zeta_k\)-involving instances, while the equality reports observed endpoints. Equivalently, the rules are sound and every reported endpoint left circular has both a tail and an arrowhead whole-family realization in \(\mathcal C(\mathcal O(\eta))\), with each realization a fully specified model sharing one basal selected DAG on \(V\cup S\) across its regimes, carrying its own kernel family with unchanged non-target kernels, supplying its own observational selected law and faithful pooled selected laws, and preserving the entire full-regime signature.
body.justification: Equality with the canonical endpoint invariant is the theorem-level structure-identification kernel.
body.gap: Dai et al., Theorem 3 and p. 8, lines 646--662, prove CDIS soundness and explicitly leave completeness open. Zhang, Sections 3--4 and Theorem 2, establishes single-PAG arrowhead and tail completeness, not common-basal synchronization. The Zhou--Kocaoglu author listing at lines 27--31 and public abstract at lines 5--9 describe known-target completion by compatible-MAG enumeration; official theorem numbering and text were inaccessible, so only the abstract-level distinction is used.
body.consumer: The theorem makes a retained A549 circle an identified equivalence-class feature rather than evidence of an unfinished orientation algorithm.
